description: A composite figure group combining a results table with a TEM micrograph. The upper image is a four-column table headed exactly "Sample condition | Grain (μm)/crystallite size (nm) | Determination method | Ref.". Its rows list Fe-6.8Al in three conditions: "98% CR" (102.3 ± 9.8, XRD analysis, Ref. "–"), "750 °C, 5 min" (25.2 ± 5.0, SEM, [15]) and "750 °C, 60 min" (48.3 ± 1.2, SEM, "–"); the column heading pools two units (μm and nm) without per-cell unit labels. The lower image is a dark-field TEM micrograph with a 200 nm scale bar, showing very fine bright ordered-phase particles, marked by red arrows, dispersed in a dark matrix and appearing aligned in bands running diagonally. The inset is a selected-area diffraction pattern showing strong matrix reflections annotated 200, 2̄11̄ and 01̄1̄ together with weaker superlattice spots highlighted by yellow arrows. The panels jointly argue that nanometre-scale ordered phase exists in the Fe-6.8Al matrix — visible as bright dark-field contrast and as weak superlattice reflections — while the table supplies the grain/crystallite sizes for the three processing conditions.

subfigures.description: A four-column table titled by its headings 'Sample condition', 'Grain (μm)/crystallite size (nm)', 'Determination method', 'Ref.'. Three data rows: 98% CR, 102.3 ± 9.8, XRD analysis, '–'; 750 °C, 5 min, 25.2 ± 5.0, SEM, [15]; 750 °C, 60 min, 48.3 ± 1.2, SEM, '–'. Numbers are printed with ± uncertainties; units are given only in the pooled column heading.

Dark-field TEM micrograph of Fe-6.8Al with a 200 nm scale bar, showing fine bright ordered-phase particles marked by red arrows against a dark background, apparently aligned in bands. An inset SAED pattern shows strong matrix spots labelled 200, 2̄11̄ and 01̄1̄ plus weaker superlattice spots indicated by yellow arrows.

observations.observation: The table row for sample condition '98% CR' gives a size of 102.3 ± 9.8 with determination method 'XRD analysis' and no reference.
The table row for '750 °C, 5 min' gives 25.2 ± 5.0 determined by SEM, citing reference [15].
The table row for '750 °C, 60 min' gives 48.3 ± 1.2 determined by SEM with no reference.
The table column heading pools two units — 'Grain (μm)/crystallite size (nm)' — so the unit (μm grain vs nm crystallite) for each individual value is not printed in the cells.
The dark-field TEM micrograph carries a 200 nm scale bar and shows bright nanometre-scale particles (indicated by red arrows) dispersed in a dark matrix.
The SAED inset contains strong matrix spots and weaker spots highlighted with yellow arrows, with reflections annotated 200, 2̄11̄ and 01̄1̄.

The caption states the inset diffraction pattern is from the [011] zone axis of the Fe-Al matrix and that the weak ordered-phase spots are highlighted by yellow arrows while ordered phase regions are marked by red arrows.
The caption states the figure shows the distribution of ordered phase in the Fe-6.8Al sample in dark-field TEM.
The citing text states the dark-field image was obtained from the 00weak diffraction spots and shows very fine ordered phase (bright) against a dark background.
The citing text states the size of the ordered phase was determined to be 2.1 ± 0.2 nm and that this correlates with the size determined from SAXS studies (cf. Fig. 4).
The citing text states the weak spots in the diffraction pattern correspond to superlattice peaks from the ordered phase, while strong spots arise from matrix [011] zone-axis reflections.
The ordered-phase particle size (2.1 ± 0.2 nm, from the citing text) is not printed anywhere in the image pixels and cannot be read off the micrograph.
